title: One-third malformed-copy tolerance under a clean-marginal bank promise

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N) and use the final bank-first algorithm with Q=192 for N=2 and Q=27648(2n+20) for N>=3, r=Q/3, t=n+18, J=n+24, M=2^(ceil(n/2)+2), and the phase-precision and fixed-point rule in proof.md Sections 0-8. For n=1 (N=2), use the fixed-size exact finite branch. For n>=2, let L=log2 n. The uniform compiler uses log2(n+2)^4, which is O(L^4) for n>=2 and is covered at n=1 by the finite branch. This same final implementation meets each stated bound on every execution branch, for every bank input allowed by claim 5 with epsilon(n)=1/3, including the clean input; the claims hold jointly with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 11/16 and the other stated resource bounds. Hidden constants are absolute and independent of N, s, the input bank and outcomes. Worst-case total sequential work is T(N,s)=O(2^(n/2)n^5 L^4), including all classical bit operations, circuit generation and inversion, gates, measurements, initialization, source cost n+1 per copy, certified gate synthesis and every indexed address charge. For n>=2 the uniform envelope is B_T(n)=2^(n/2)n^5(log2 n)^4, with growth index exactly 1.

The total number of fresh acquired source copies on every execution branch is exactly Q(N,s)=192 for N=2 and Q(N,s)=27648(2n+20) for N>=3, hence Q=O(n). There are no further source calls, failed source attempts or restarts. Its uniform sample envelope B_samples(n)=n has growth index exactly 0.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N) and use the final bank-first algorithm with Q=192 for N=2 and Q=27648(2n+20) for N>=3, r=Q/3, t=n+18, J=n+24, M=2^(ceil(n/2)+2), and the phase-precision and fixed-point rule in proof.md Sections 0-8. All Q registers arrive before any algorithm measurement, private random draw, source transformation or abort. For n=1 (N=2), use the fixed-size exact finite branch. For n>=2, let L=log2 n. The uniform compiler uses log2(n+2)^4, which is O(L^4) for n>=2 and is covered at n=1 by the finite branch. For a fixed but unknown set B of at most r registers, let G be its complement and sigma be the bank state. The promise is Tr_B sigma=rho_s^(tensor G), where rho_s=(1/N) sum_x |psi_(x,s)><psi_(x,s)| and |psi_(x,s)>=(|0,x>+|1,(x+s) mod N>)/sqrt(2). The state on B is arbitrary and may be entangled with G; any purification reference is inaccessible. The guarantee also holds for convex mixtures of such fixed-B inputs. The algorithm does not know B, and the source cannot access the bank or workspace after acquisition. This is a batch clean-marginal promise, not an interactive replacement service. For every such input, including B empty, the algorithm outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 11/16. On every execution branch, the same algorithm jointly has T=O(2^(n/2)n^5 L^4), S_C=O(n), S_Q=O(n^2), and exactly Q acquired source copies, hence Q=O(n). All hidden constants are absolute and independent of N, s, the input bank and outcomes.

structured.error_model: Among the Q acquired copies, an adversary fixes a set B of at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) malformed positions, possibly depending on N and s. The joint state is arbitrary subject to its reduced state on all other positions being exactly rho_s^{tensor (Q-|B|)}. Malformed systems may be correlated or entangled with each other and with other systems subject to that marginal promise. No source control, purification access, or preparation inverse is supplied.
